page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 storage-focused instance designed specifically for big data workloads requiring dense local storage capacity. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor providing 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via hyper-threading. The instance is allocated 32.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU) and features 33 MB of L3 cache alongside baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

A defining characteristic of the ecs.d1ne.2xlarge is its massive bundle of 23,622 GB of local HDD storage. This architecture prioritizes mass data capacity directly attached to the host, trading the high random IOPS and low latency of NVMe or SSD options for extensive raw storage volume.

Benchmark results highlight computational and throughput constraints stemming from the legacy Intel Broadwell architecture. Single-core stress-ng (1107.49) and Geekbench single-core (964.0) fall into the bottom 25% of evaluated cloud servers, while multi-core metrics like Geekbench multi-core (3578.0) and stress-ng multi-core (5886.32) reflect similar entry-tier compute limits. Memory performance tests, such as PassMark memory (1665.11) and large-block read bandwidth (39.05 GB/sec), demonstrate standard legacy DDR4 throughput. Web serving throughput sits at 4.64 GB/sec, and LLM inference on medium 7B models operates at lower processing speeds (10.06 tokens/sec prompt, 4.83 tokens/sec generation).

Given the lower relative compute capability combined with vast storage density, this instance offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for batch-oriented storage needs rather than real-time computing. It is best applied to distributed storage clusters, Hadoop/HDFS nodes, log aggregation archives, cold or warm data lakes, and sequential ETL processes where raw HDD volume outweighs single-threaded compute demands.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.2xlarge is a big data and storage-oriented server featuring an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz across 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs. Equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory and a 6 Gbps baseline network interface, its primary hardware highlight is a massive local storage capacity consisting of 23,622 GB of HDD storage. No GPU acceleration is present. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate modest compute efficiency, with Geekbench single-core at 964.0 and multi-core at 3578.0, alongside moderate uncached memory write bandwidth of 35.66 GB/sec. Given its hardware profile, the instance prioritizes raw spindle-based storage density over compute throughput. The ecs.d1ne.2xlarge is technically appropriate for distributed file systems such as Hadoop HDFS, sequential ETL pipelines, centralized log storage, and data archiving tasks.
